tools.name: get_status
tools.title: get status
tools.description: Get the current Blockbench state: open project, format, counts of cubes/groups/textures/animations, and edit mode. Call this first to understand the workspace. If you are about to BUILD or TEXTURE a model, call get_guide first. REFERENCES FIRST: if the subject is a known character, creature, franchise item, vehicle, building or real product, ask the user for reference images (Blockwright has no web image search), load the best 2-4 with load_reference {path} or {data_url}, then make_palette from them. If the user dropped a reference into the MCP Copilot panel, call get_reference to see it. Build, then compare_reference every pass until match_percent is high — do not judge the match by eye.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.title: get guide
tools.description: Return a playbook. Pass `topic`: 'modeling' (default — proportions, detail, rotation), 'detailing' (the cube budgets and the 4-layer doctrine that stop models coming out as 15 boxes — read it before building anything with a costume, armour or cloth), 'orientation' (which side is the model's LEFT — read before anything with a left and a right), 'rigging' (bone hierarchy, joint origins, why 2-bone limbs animate like cardboard), 'texturing' (the smooth @volmur/Hytale look), 'vfx' (pixelated flames/energy/projectiles), 'animation' (axis signs, gaits, easing, the measure-then-review loop), 'review' (how to get the user to confirm work instead of declaring it good yourself), 'reference' (how to ACTUALLY match a reference image, find more references on the web and build the palette), 'character' (anime/stylised characters: proportions, face, hair, cloth, the generator recipe), 'mechanism' (gears, pistons, pipes and animating them) or 'inspection' (how to find and fix the small things screenshots miss). READ the relevant topic BEFORE building/rigging/texturing/animating — it dramatically improves results.

tools.name: get_orientation
tools.title: get orientation
tools.description: THE left/right authority for this model — call it before rigging, mirroring, attaching an item to a hand, or interpreting any render. Returns which way the model faces and which world axis is the model's OWN right and left (Minecraft models face -Z, so the model's right is +X), plus the trap that causes most mistakes: a front-view render shows the model MIRRORED (its right hand appears on the LEFT of the image), exactly like facing a person. Also returns the rotation-sign cheat sheet (+X swings a hanging limb FORWARD, tips an upright torso BACKWARD; +Y turns the model to its own left).

tools.title: which side

tools.title: check sides

Catches the classic failures: a bone called arm_right sitting on the model's left, a mirrored pair that ended up on the same side, and limbs with no counterpart. Run it after building or mirroring anything symmetric, and again before you tell the user a left/right request is done.

tools.name: request_review
tools.title: request review
tools.description: SHOW THE USER and WAIT for their verdict — the honest alternative to looking at your own screenshot and declaring it good. Renders labelled views (or animation poses) and posts them as a card in the MCP Copilot panel inside Blockbench, then waits a SHORT window for the user to press 'Looks right' / 'Needs changes' and optionally type a comment. If they haven't answered yet it returns `pending: true` with a `review_id` — the card stays open, so call wait_review with that id to keep waiting (that loop is how a minutes-long human review fits inside an MCP client's per-request timeout). Call it after every user-visible milestone: the blockout, the texture pass, EACH animation, anything the user asked for specifically, and before you claim a task is finished. Run the objective checks (check_model / check_sides / check_rig / analyze_animation) FIRST — don't spend the user's attention on something a tool would have caught. If the answer is 'needs changes', fix exactly what they said and ask again. `pending` and a timeout are NOT approval.

tools.name: compare_reference
tools.title: compare reference
tools.description: THE reference-matching tool — turns 'does it match?' into a measured number so you stop building blind. Renders your model from the chosen angle on a transparent background, extracts the model + reference SILHOUETTES, normalises them (so scale/position in the viewport don't matter) and returns: match_percent (silhouette IoU 0-100), aspect_delta_pct (model too wide/narrow), ref_only_pct (reference area with NO model under it = MISSING mass), model_only_pct (model beyond the reference = EXTRA mass), a verdict + concrete advice, AND a composite image [reference | your model | overlay]. In the overlay RED = reference-only (add mass there), BLUE = model-only (trim), WHITE = match. Aim the camera to the reference angle first (set_camera_angle/screenshot_views) or pass `view`. Call this EVERY modeling pass and iterate until match_percent >= 85 — do not declare a match by eye.

reference.description: Reference id/name/index to compare against (default: the most recent).
reference.markdownDescription: Reference id/name/index to compare against (default: the most recent).

view.description: Camera preset to render from ('front','back','left','right','isometric_right_front',...). Omit to use the current view (aim it first). Models usually face -Z, so 'back' shows the creature's face.
view.markdownDescription: Camera preset to render from ('front','back','left','right','isometric_right_front',...). Omit to use the current view (aim it first). Models usually face -Z, so 'back' shows the creature's face.

threshold.description: Alpha cutoff 0..1 for the model silhouette (default 0.45).
threshold.markdownDescription: Alpha cutoff 0..1 for the model silhouette (default 0.45).

Use it to match a reference NUMERICALLY (e.g. 'head should be ~1/4 of total height') — complements compare_reference's silhouette score. tools.name: add_cube
tools.title: add cube
tools.description: Add a cube to the model. Place it the way you think about it instead of hand-computing corners: `center`+`size`, or `attach` it to a face of an existing cube (`attach:{to:'torso', face:'front', at:[0,0.4], embed:0.2}` + `size` — it lands ON that surface, follows the target's rotation and bone, and never floats), or classic `from`/`to`. `mirror:true` also builds the twin on the other side (names get _right/_left). Cubes support `rotation` (degrees) and `inflate` (round/shrink without moving). The model faces -Z, so its OWN right is +X — pass `side` and the tool will enforce it. Coplanar faces it creates are fixed automatically. Prefer add_cubes for many cubes.

center.description: Centre [x,y,z] — use with `size` instead of from/to.
center.markdownDescription: Centre [x,y,z] — use with `size` instead of from/to.

size.description: Size [w,h,d] — with `center`, or with `attach` (in the target cube's own axes).
size.markdownDescription: Size [w,h,d] — with `center`, or with `attach` (in the target cube's own axes).

attach.description: Stick the cube onto a face of another cube: {to:'<cube name>', face:'front'|'back'|'left'|'right'|'top'|'bottom'|north/south/east/west/up/down, at:[a,b] position on that face from -1 to 1 (0,0 = centre; north/south faces: [x,y], east/west: [z,y], up/down: [x,z]), embed: how far it sinks in (default 0; 0.1-0.3 hides seams), offset:[x,y,z] extra shift}. Requires `size`. Carries the target's rotation/bone, so details on a rotated plate sit flush.
attach.markdownDescription: Stick the cube onto a face of another cube: {to:'<cube name>', face:'front'|'back'|'left'|'right'|'top'|'bottom'|north/south/east/west/up/down, at:[a,b] position on that face from -1 to 1 (0,0 = centre; north/south faces: [x,y], east/west: [z,y], up/down: [x,z]), embed: how far it sinks in (default 0; 0.1-0.3 hides seams), offset:[x,y,z] extra shift}. Requires `size`. Carries the target's rotation/bone, so details on a rotated plate sit flush.

mirror.description: Also create the mirrored twin across the model's centre line (names get _right/_left from where each lands).
mirror.markdownDescription: Also create the mirrored twin across the model's centre line (names get _right/_left from where each lands).

fix_z_fighting.markdownDescription: Automatically resolve the coplanar faces this call creates (default true): the smaller cube of each pair gets a tiny inflate, UVs untouched. The result reports z_fight_fixed. Pass false only to inspect the raw overlaps.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees [x,y,z]. Single-axis is most reliable per cube.
rotation.markdownDescription: Rotation in degrees [x,y,z]. Single-axis is most reliable per cube.

inflate.description: Inflate (+) or shrink (-) all faces in place — use for rounding/taper.
inflate.markdownDescription: Inflate (+) or shrink (-) all faces in place — use for rounding/taper.

box_uv.description: Use box UV (default follows the format).
box_uv.markdownDescription: Use box UV (default follows the format).

parent.description: uuid or name of the parent group.
parent.markdownDescription: uuid or name of the parent group.

tools.title: add groups
tools.description: Create many bones/groups in one call — the fast way to lay out a whole skeleton. Pass `groups`: an array of {name, origin, rotation, parent}. A group's `parent` may reference another group created earlier in the SAME call by name, so you can build a nested, pre-posed bone hierarchy at once.

groups.markdownDescription: Array of group specs: {name, origin:[x,y,z], rotation:[x,y,z], parent:name|uuid}.

tools.name: add_cubes
tools.title: add cubes
tools.description: Create many cubes in one call — the efficient way to author a detailed model. BUDGET: a simple prop is 30-60 cubes, a standard mob/NPC 100-180, a hero model 180-300+; a humanoid built from under ~70 cubes is a draft, not a model (audit_complexity enforces this). Hand-computing [from,to] is what you are worst at, so use this for the primary masses and reach for the generators for the rest: add_hollow_volume (hoods/helmets/armour shells), generate_array (hems, scales, plates, teeth, rivets), extrude_chain (horns, tails, tentacles), add_wing (bat/dragon wings with a continuous membrane), voxelize_matrix (blades, emblems, flat detail). Pass `cubes`: an array where each item takes the same fields as add_cube ({name, from, to, center, size, attach, mirror, origin, rotation, inflate, parent, side, box_uv, uv_offset, faces}); `attach.to` may name a cube created earlier in the same array, so you can build a part and its details in one call. Use mirror:true instead of hand-mirroring. Build symmetric parts by emitting both the left side and its mirror (negate X, flip Y/Z rotation signs) in the same array, and tag each with side:'left'/'right' — the model faces -Z so its OWN right is +X, and the whole batch is validated before anything is created, so a mirrored limb fails loudly instead of silently. Coplanar faces created by the batch are fixed automatically (z_fight_fixed in the result); still make overlapping parts clearly penetrate each other (>=0.1). Returns all created cubes with their face UVs.

cubes.description: Array of cube specs (each like add_cube's args).
cubes.markdownDescription: Array of cube specs (each like add_cube's args).

fix_z_fighting.description: Automatically resolve the coplanar faces this call creates (default true): the smaller cube of each pair gets a tiny inflate, UVs untouched. The result reports z_fight_fixed. Pass false only to inspect the raw overlaps.
fix_z_fighting.markdownDescription: Automatically resolve the coplanar faces this call creates (default true): the smaller cube of each pair gets a tiny inflate, UVs untouched. The result reports z_fight_fixed. Pass false only to inspect the raw overlaps.

tools.name: voxelize_matrix
tools.title: voxelize matrix
tools.description: DRAW a shape as a character matrix and get 3D cubes back — the fix for parts you cannot compute [from,to] for by hand. You are excellent at 2D pixel art and bad at 3D arithmetic, so describe the SILHOUETTE in rows of characters and this extrudes it. Universal: sword/scythe/axe blades, bows, horns, shield emblems, fins, flat wings, chevrons, keys, gears, plate patterns, tattered banner edges. `matrix` rows are top-to-bottom, ' ' and '.' are empty; every other character becomes cubes. Per character, `palette` sets {name (drives detail_cubes colour rules), depth (thickness in units), offset_z (shift along the depth axis — layer a rim in front of a core), inflate}. `plane` picks the projection: 'xy' front view (columns->+X, rows descend -Y, depth along +Z), 'xz' top view (columns->+X, rows go back-to-front, depth along +Y), 'yz' side view (columns->+Z with column 0 at the model's FRONT, rows descend -Y, depth along +X). `origin` is the grid's minimum corner. `merge_adjacent:true` merges runs of the same character across a row into one cube (far fewer cubes, same shape). Then pack_uv.

fix_z_fighting.markdownDescription: Automatically resolve the coplanar faces this call creates (default true): the smaller cube of each pair gets a tiny inflate, UVs untouched. The result reports z_fight_fixed. Pass false only to inspect the raw overlaps.

tools.name: add_hollow_volume
tools.title: add hollow volume
tools.description: Build a SHELL instead of a solid box — the fix for the single biggest 'AI model' tell, a monolithic cube where a hollow form belongs. Creates up to six walls of `wall_thickness` around an empty cavity, skipping every direction in `open_faces`. Universal: hoods (open 'north'+'down' so the face and neck show), helmets, masks, visors, eye sockets, breastplates, pauldrons, bracers, collars, cages, wheels, pipes, chimneys, crates, troughs. Faces are WORLD-relative — north=-Z (the model's front), south=+Z, east=+X, west=-X, up, down — and the model-relative words front/back/left/right/top/bottom are accepted too. The walls tile the shell exactly, so they never overlap or z-fight each other; anything you place INSIDE the cavity should still keep >=0.1 clearance from them. Returns the cavity bounds so you can fill it.

tools.name: generate_array
tools.title: generate array
tools.description: Repeat one element along a line, around a ring, or over a grid — the fix for parts you would otherwise collapse into one flat box. Universal: torn/shingled hems on cloaks and skirts, scales, feathers, overlapping armour plates, teeth in a jaw, spikes along a spine, rivets, fence posts, chain links, ribs, tassels. `mode:'linear'` needs start+end, `'radial'` needs center+radii (an ellipse in XZ, elements turned to face outward by default), `'grid'` needs start+end plus counts (or count). `anchor` decides how each element sits on its point: 'center' (default), 'top' (element HANGS from the point — use for fringes), 'bottom' (stands on it — spikes), 'min'. `jitter` breaks the machine-regular look, `size_decay` grows/shrinks elements along the run (per-step delta in units, negative to taper), `rotation_range` {min,max} gives each element its own tilt, and `depth_stagger` alternates neighbours in depth so overlapping rows CANNOT z-fight — always pass 0.05-0.2 for shingled rows. `seed` makes the randomness repeatable. The result reports `z_fight_pairs`: elements whose faces ended up on the same plane anyway (a row where each element overlaps two others still lines up), with the fix to apply — act on it rather than leaving it for check_model.

fix_z_fighting.markdownDescription: Automatically resolve the coplanar faces this call creates (default true): the smaller cube of each pair gets a tiny inflate, UVs untouched. The result reports z_fight_fixed. Pass false only to inspect the raw overlaps.

tools.name: extrude_chain
tools.title: extrude chain
tools.description: Build a tapering, curving chain of segments — optionally one BONE per segment, so it can be animated. Universal: tentacles, horns, antlers, claws, curved tails, tusks, branches, snake bodies, hair braids, cables, antennae, whip links. The chain grows along `direction` from `base_origin`; each segment is `taper`-thinner than the last and each bone adds `curvature` degrees on top of its parent, so segment i sits at base_rotation + i x curvature and the whole thing sweeps into a curve. With `create_bones:true` (default) the segments nest as a bone chain — that is what gives a tail follow-through and a tentacle its whip; the rest pose is laid out straight and the bone rotations produce the curve. With `create_bones:false` the rotations are baked into the cubes and it cannot be animated (and single-axis-rotation formats such as java_block will not honour compound angles). Returns `tip`, the world position where the chain ends, so you can attach something there.

tools.description: THE detail gate — run it before you texture anything, and act on the verdict. It measures whether the model is actually built or is still a blockout wearing a costume: total cube count against a budget (simple prop 30-60, standard mob/NPC 100-180, hero/boss 180-300+), MONOLITHIC boxes (one cube holding >30% of the model's volume with nothing layered on it — the classic 'one cube per torso, one cube per cloak'), layering (how much geometry overlaps other geometry at all), micro-detail density (cubes <=2 units), bare slabs (a large face with nothing on or near it), bone-hierarchy depth, and how much is rotated. Returns `verdict`: 'too_primitive' (under budget — a humanoid under ~80 cubes is a draft, not a model), 'acceptable' or 'high_detail', plus `ready_for_texturing` and a concrete fix per issue. A high cube count with no layering still looks flat, so pair this with compare_reference (silhouette) and check_model (z-fighting, untextured faces).

tools.name: detail_cubes
tools.title: detail cubes
tools.description: The texturing engine. Every pixel is computed from the 3D point it lands on: hue-shifted light (cool shadows, warm lights — not a brightness multiplier), ambient occlusion where parts meet or tuck under others, 1px bevel highlights on edges, darkening toward the ground, and per-MATERIAL surface detail (cloth folds, hair strands + an anime shine band, metal sheen + scratches, wood grain, stone cracks, leather stitching, scales, glowing emissive). Patterns are laid out in world space so they continue across neighbouring cubes: plaid/tartan, stripes, checker, dots, panels (+rivets), grille/vents, hazard, bricks, planks, scales, trim/lace borders (solid, zigzag, dashed) on chosen edges, gradients, speckle. Rules match cube names (regex); colours may be palette keys from make_palette ('$hair', '$skirt.shadow'). Run pack_uv and create_texture first; re-run after changing geometry (the shading comes from it). Then paint_face for the face and paint_faces for any other crisp marking. style:'smooth' gives the old soft-gradient look.

materials.description: Rules, first match wins: [{match:'^hair', material:'hair', color:'$hair'}, {match:'skirt', material:'cloth', color:'#b3262d', pattern:[{type:'plaid', color:'#1b1b1f', size:4}, {type:'lace', edges:'bottom', width:2, style:'zigzag', color:'#ffffff'}]}, {match:'buckle', material:'metal', color:'#c9cdd2'}]. material: matte, skin, cloth, leather, metal, gold, wood, stone, hair, fur, plastic, rubber, glass, crystal, foliage, bone, scales, emissive (guessed from the cube name when omitted). Per-rule overrides: contrast, bevel, noise, hue_shift, shadow_hue, light_hue, shadow_sat, ao, folds, strands, shine, sheen, scratches, grain, cracks, stitch, emissive. Pattern fields: type, color, color2, size, band, line, twill, spacing, rivets, rivet_color, width, edges ('all'|'top'|'bottom'|'side'), style ('solid'|'zigzag'|'dashed'), direction, start, strength, amount, density, offset, space ('world'|'face').

tools.name: add_keyframes
tools.title: add keyframes
tools.description: Add many keyframes at once — the way to author or refine a full animation. Pass an array of {bone, channel, time, value, interpolation}. SIGNS (model faces -Z): +X rotation swings a DOWN-pointing bone (arm/leg) FORWARD and tips an UP-pointing bone (torso/neck/head) BACKWARD; elbows bend +X, knees bend -X; +Y turns the model toward its own LEFT. Aim for 6-9 keyframes per moving bone and animate the LOWER limb segments too, or it reads as cardboard. Use interpolation 'catmullrom' for swings/settles and 'linear' only for impact snaps. Set close_loop:true on a cycle so the end pose exactly matches t=0. Nothing is written unless every bone name resolves. After this, ALWAYS run analyze_animation.

tools.name: create_rig
tools.title: create rig
tools.description: Build a proper animation skeleton in one call — the fix for stiff, cardboard animation. Creates a full bone hierarchy with THREE segments per limb (upper / lower / hand-or-foot) so elbows and knees can actually bend, joint origins exactly on the pivots, a segmented spine + neck + head (+ optional jaw and tail chain), and correct *_left / *_right naming for the model's OWN sides. By default it also drops in a blocked-out placeholder body you reshape with edit_element and then add detail cubes into. Do this BEFORE modelling if the creature will be animated — retro-fitting an elbow into a finished 2-bone arm is far more work.

height.markdownDescription: Total height in units for a humanoid / shoulder height for a quadruped (humanoid default 32 = a Minecraft player).

scale.markdownDescription: Extra uniform scale on top of `height`.

offset.markdownDescription: Move the whole rig by [x,y,z] (e.g. to stand it on a different origin).

arm_segments.markdownDescription: 2 = upper+lower, 3 = +hand (default 3). Fewer than 3 means no wrist.

spine_segments.description: 1-3 torso bones between hips and chest (default 2).
spine_segments.markdownDescription: 1-3 torso bones between hips and chest (default 2).

tail_segments.description: Tail chain length (humanoid default 0, quadruped 3). Tails carry follow-through.
tail_segments.markdownDescription: Tail chain length (humanoid default 0, quadruped 3). Tails carry follow-through.

placeholder_cubes.markdownDescription: Also create a blocked-out body in each bone (default true).

tools.name: check_rig
tools.title: check rig
tools.description: Audit the skeleton BEFORE animating and fix what it reports. Catches exactly what makes AI animation look bad: limbs with fewer than 3 segments (no elbow/knee — the cardboard look), bone origins sitting in the middle of a limb instead of on the joint (the part spins instead of swinging), cubes not parented to a bone, missing root/spine/head, left-right naming that contradicts the geometry, and suspiciously low bone counts. Returns ready_to_animate plus a concrete fix for every issue.

tools.name: get_rig
tools.title: get rig
tools.description: Return the skeleton as the animation tools understand it: which bones are the spine/neck/head/tail, and each limb's segment chain with its detected side. Use it to see whether your naming is being picked up before you generate or hand-write an animation.

tools.name: generate_animation
tools.title: generate animation
tools.description: Generate a complete, direction-correct base animation from the rig — then refine it. It reads the skeleton, applies the correct rotation SIGNS for the way the model faces (so an attack swings forward, not into its own back), bends elbows forward and knees backward, offsets phases for a proper gait, counter-rotates hips against chest, adds body bob, head stabilisation and tail follow-through, and closes loops seamlessly. Types: 'idle' (breathing + weight shift), 'walk', 'run', 'attack' (anticipation → strike → contact hold → recovery; pick the `hand`), 'cast', 'jump', 'hurt', 'death', 'fly'. Handles humanoid and quadruped rigs. Treat the result as a strong first pass: run analyze_animation, refine with add_keyframes, preview_animation, then request_review.

length.description: Length in seconds (sensible default per type: idle 4, walk 1, run 0.62, attack 0.85).
length.markdownDescription: Length in seconds (sensible default per type: idle 4, walk 1, run 0.62, attack 0.85).

intensity.description: Amplitude multiplier 0.2-2.5 (default 1). Raise for exaggerated/heavy creatures.
intensity.markdownDescription: Amplitude multiplier 0.2-2.5 (default 1). Raise for exaggerated/heavy creatures.

hand.description: Which hand attacks (default 'right' — the model's OWN right).
hand.markdownDescription: Which hand attacks (default 'right' — the model's OWN right).

direction.markdownDescription: Which way a death fall goes (default backward).

replace.markdownDescription: Replace an existing animation of the same name (default true).

tools.name: analyze_animation
tools.title: analyze animation
tools.description: MEASURE an animation instead of eyeballing it — this is what catches 'the attack swings backwards'. It evaluates the rig at sampled times and reports, for every hand/foot/head/tail tip, how far it actually travels FORWARD / BACK / LEFT / RIGHT / UP in the model's own axes and when, plus: whether a loop closes, keyframe counts per bone, all-linear interpolation, and limbs whose lower segment never moves while the upper one swings (the cardboard tell). For strike-like animations it explicitly verdicts the direction. Run it after every generate_animation and after hand-writing keyframes, fix what it reports, then re-run.

animation.markdownDescription: uuid or name of the animation.

samples.markdownDescription: How many times to sample across the animation (default 16).

tools.title: preview animation

Each image is stamped with the time, the view, and which edge of the image is the model's right. Pair it with analyze_animation (the numbers) and request_review (the human verdict).

animation.markdownDescription: uuid or name of the animation.

times.markdownDescription: Times in seconds (default 0/25/50/75% of the length).

views.markdownDescription: Model-relative views per pose (default ['front_right']). 'left' is a good second view for gaits.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the 3D preview as an image. Pass `view` to aim the camera in one step (model-relative: 'front' looks at its FACE, 'back', 'left'/'right' = the side its left/right arm is on, 'front_right', 'top'). Every capture is stamped with what it shows and WHICH EDGE OF THE IMAGE is the model's own right — a front view is mirrored, so its right hand appears on the image's left. Read that stamp instead of guessing sides. A screenshot is for YOUR iteration; it is not verification — use request_review for that.

view.markdownDescription: Model-relative view to aim at first. Omit to use the current camera.

tools.name: screenshot_views
tools.title: screenshot views
tools.description: Capture several camera angles in ONE call — PLUS close-ups of the spots where something is wrong or most likely to be wrong (z-fighting, floating parts, hidden cubes, left/right mix-ups, then the face, hands, feet, joints and gear contacts), each framed tight, with what stands in front clipped away and the cubes involved outlined and labelled. Views are named from the MODEL's point of view — 'front' shows its FACE, 'left' is the side its left arm is on — and each image is stamped with which edge is the model's right, because front views are mirrored. Defaults to front_right/front/left/back + up to 4 close-ups. STUDY the close-ups: they are where models break. Do this after each pass, then request_review so the USER confirms it.

views.description: Views in order. Each item is a model-relative name ('front','back','left','right','top','bottom','front_right','front_left','back_right','back_left'), a world axis ('+x','-z','north','east'), or a {position:[x,y,z], target:[x,y,z]} object. Omit for a sensible default set.

tools.name: set_ik_controller
tools.title: Set IK Controller
tools.description: Creates or updates an inverse-kinematics controller. Blockbench drives IK from a null object: ik_target is the end effector (group/bone, armature bone, or locator) that reaches for the null object, ik_source is the chain root (defaults to the null object's parent), ik_pole (Blockbench 5.2+) sets the bend direction, and lock_ik_target_rotation keeps the effector's rotation. Works with bone rigs and armatures (5.2 allows null objects under armatures and armature bones). Validates every reference and that the target lies below the chain root; returns the solved chain. Replaces the deprecated bone_rigging set_ik flags, which Blockbench never read.

null_object.description: UUID or name of an existing null object to update. Omit to create a new IK controller null object.
null_object.markdownDescription: UUID or name of an existing null object to update. Omit to create a new IK controller null object.

name.description: Name for the null object. Defaults to '<ik_target name>_ik' when creating.
name.markdownDescription: Name for the null object. Defaults to '<ik_target name>_ik' when creating.

position.description: Null object position [x, y, z] as Blockbench stores it (model space for root and group parents). Defaults to the end effector's world pivot when creating.
position.markdownDescription: Null object position [x, y, z] as Blockbench stores it (model space for root and group parents). Defaults to the end effector's world pivot when creating.

parent.description: Parent group, armature, or armature bone (UUID or name), or 'root'. Defaults to root when creating. When ik_source is empty the parent is the implicit chain root, so keep IK controllers outside the chain they drive.
parent.markdownDescription: Parent group, armature, or armature bone (UUID or name), or 'root'. Defaults to root when creating. When ik_source is empty the parent is the implicit chain root, so keep IK controllers outside the chain they drive.

ik_target.description: End effector that reaches for the null object: a group/bone, armature bone, or locator (UUID or name). Required when creating; must be a descendant of the chain root. Empty string clears.
ik_target.markdownDescription: End effector that reaches for the null object: a group/bone, armature bone, or locator (UUID or name). Required when creating; must be a descendant of the chain root. Empty string clears.

ik_source.description: Chain root: a group/bone or armature bone (UUID or name). The chain spans from here down to ik_target. Empty string clears, making the null object's parent the chain root.
ik_source.markdownDescription: Chain root: a group/bone or armature bone (UUID or name). The chain spans from here down to ik_target. Empty string clears, making the null object's parent the chain root.

ik_pole.description: Pole target controlling the bend direction (Blockbench 5.2+): a group, locator, or other null object (UUID or name). Empty string clears.
ik_pole.markdownDescription: Pole target controlling the bend direction (Blockbench 5.2+): a group, locator, or other null object (UUID or name). Empty string clears.

lock_ik_target_rotation.description: Keep the end effector's world rotation while the chain solves.
lock_ik_target_rotation.markdownDescription: Keep the end effector's world rotation while the chain solves.

tools.name: get_display_transform

slot.markdownDescription: Display slot to read. If omitted, returns every populated slot in the project.

tools.name: set_display_transform
tools.title: Set Display Transform
tools.description: Writes a Java Edition display slot's transform (translation, rotation, scale, mirror, pivots). Creates the slot if it does not exist yet (seeded from Blockbench's Bedrock item display defaults on bedrock_block projects, identity otherwise) and wraps the change in an undo step. This edits data that ships in the exported model JSON — it changes the deliverable, not just the preview. Values are kept as given, like Blockbench does; outside bedrock_block projects the result warns about those Minecraft Java clamps or ignores (translation beyond ±80, scale beyond ±4, pivots, the embedded slot). Requires a format that supports display mode (e.g. Java Block/Item).

slot.description: Display slot to modify. embedded is a Bedrock block slot that Minecraft Java ignores.
slot.markdownDescription: Display slot to modify. embedded is a Bedrock block slot that Minecraft Java ignores.

translation.description: Translation offset as [x, y, z] (Minecraft display units, 1/16 block). Minecraft Java clamps each component to ±80.
translation.markdownDescription: Translation offset as [x, y, z] (Minecraft display units, 1/16 block). Minecraft Java clamps each component to ±80.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees as [x, y, z].
rotation.markdownDescription: Rotation in degrees as [x, y, z].

scale.description: Scale factor as [x, y, z]; a negative component mirrors that axis. Minecraft Java clamps each exported component to ±4.
scale.markdownDescription: Scale factor as [x, y, z]; a negative component mirrors that axis. Minecraft Java clamps each exported component to ±4.

rotation_pivot.description: Rotation pivot point as [x, y, z]. Only Bedrock reads pivots; Minecraft Java ignores them.
rotation_pivot.markdownDescription: Rotation pivot point as [x, y, z]. Only Bedrock reads pivots; Minecraft Java ignores them.

scale_pivot.description: Scale pivot point as [x, y, z]. Only Bedrock reads pivots; Minecraft Java ignores them.
scale_pivot.markdownDescription: Scale pivot point as [x, y, z]. Only Bedrock reads pivots; Minecraft Java ignores them.

mirror.description: Per-axis mirror flags as [x, y, z].
mirror.markdownDescription: Per-axis mirror flags as [x, y, z].

reset.description: Reset the slot to its default transform before applying any of the other values: identity, or Blockbench's Bedrock defaults on bedrock_block projects.
reset.markdownDescription: Reset the slot to its default transform before applying any of the other values: identity, or Blockbench's Bedrock defaults on bedrock_block projects.

mesh_id.markdownDescription: ID or name of the mesh.

threshold.markdownDescription: Maximum distance between vertices to merge.

rotation.markdownDescription: 3D vector [x, y, z].

texture.description: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.
texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.

face.markdownDescription: Face key to attach the point to.

tools.title: Create Polyhedron

detail.markdownDescription: Subdivision level: each base triangle becomes (detail + 1)^2 triangles projected onto the sphere. 0 is the plain solid.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees.
rotation.markdownDescription: Rotation in degrees.

texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID or name to apply to every face.

group.markdownDescription: Group/bone to which the meshes belong.

tools.name: loop_cut_mesh
tools.title: Loop Cut Mesh
tools.description: Runs Blockbench's native Loop Cut on a mesh: splits the quad ring crossing the start edge with one or more parallel cuts, with offset, direction and 5.2 spacing modes (proportional, even_start, even_end). One undo entry. The new loop vertices become the selection and are returned.

mesh_id.description: ID or name of the mesh. If not provided, uses selected mesh.
mesh_id.markdownDescription: ID or name of the mesh. If not provided, uses selected mesh.

edge.description: Two vertex keys of the edge to start the loop from; the cut runs across the face ring perpendicular to it. Defaults to the mesh's current vertex/face selection (at least two selected vertices).
edge.markdownDescription: Two vertex keys of the edge to start the loop from; the cut runs across the face ring perpendicular to it. Defaults to the mesh's current vertex/face selection (at least two selected vertices).

offset.description: Distance of the (first) cut from the start of the edge, in the given unit. Defaults to the edge midpoint (or even spacing for multiple cuts).
offset.markdownDescription: Distance of the (first) cut from the start of the edge, in the given unit. Defaults to the edge midpoint (or even spacing for multiple cuts).

unit.description: Unit of offset: model units ('size') or percent of the start edge length.
unit.markdownDescription: Unit of offset: model units ('size') or percent of the start edge length.

direction.description: Rotates which edge of the start face the loop starts from, as the native Direction slider.
direction.markdownDescription: Rotates which edge of the start face the loop starts from, as the native Direction slider.

spacing.description: Blockbench 5.2 spacing: proportional keeps the same ratio on every edge of the loop; even_start/even_end keep the same absolute distance from the loop's start/end side.
spacing.markdownDescription: Blockbench 5.2 spacing: proportional keeps the same ratio on every edge of the loop; even_start/even_end keep the same absolute distance from the loop's start/end side.

tools.name: flip_in_place
tools.title: Flip In Place
tools.description: Mirrors elements in place along an axis using Blockbench's native Flip In Place (flip_in_place_x/y/z): cubes flip around their own center, meshes around their origin, groups also invert rotations in bone-rig formats. For meshes in vertex/edge/face selection mode only the selected components flip. Edit mode only.

ids.description: Element or group UUIDs/names to flip. Replaces the selection with these. Defaults to the current selection.
ids.markdownDescription: Element or group UUIDs/names to flip. Replaces the selection with these. Defaults to the current selection.

axis.description: Axis to mirror across each element's own center (cubes) or pivot (meshes, groups, other elements).
axis.markdownDescription: Axis to mirror across each element's own center (cubes) or pivot (meshes, groups, other elements).

tools.name: get_mesh_info
tools.title: Get Mesh Info
tools.description: Inspects a mesh by UUID/name or the first selected mesh without changing geometry, selection, or undo history. Returns transforms, parent, total counts, mesh-local bounds, selection counts, and optional paginated vertices/faces with actual runtime keys. Faces use perimeter vertex order and normalized mesh-local normals (zero for degenerate faces), stored texture references, and optional UVs. Texture status distinguishes resolved, missing, unassigned (false), disabled (null), and unset; default format materials are not resolved. Pages sort keys lexicographically and expose next_offset; geometry must remain unchanged between calls. Set include_vertices/include_faces false for a compact summary.

mesh_id.description: Mesh UUID or name. Omit to inspect the first selected mesh.
mesh_id.markdownDescription: Mesh UUID or name. Omit to inspect the first selected mesh.

include_vertices.description: Include a page of vertex keys, local positions, and selection flags.
include_vertices.markdownDescription: Include a page of vertex keys, local positions, and selection flags.

include_faces.description: Include a page of face keys, perimeter vertices, local normals, texture references, and selection flags.
include_faces.markdownDescription: Include a page of face keys, perimeter vertices, local normals, texture references, and selection flags.

include_uv.description: Include per-vertex UV coordinates for returned faces, in Blockbench texture units.
include_uv.markdownDescription: Include per-vertex UV coordinates for returned faces, in Blockbench texture units.

vertex_offset.description: Zero-based offset into lexicographically sorted vertex keys.
vertex_offset.markdownDescription: Zero-based offset into lexicographically sorted vertex keys.

face_offset.description: Zero-based offset into lexicographically sorted face keys.
face_offset.markdownDescription: Zero-based offset into lexicographically sorted face keys.

limit.description: Maximum items in each included page. Continue using that page's next_offset; avoid editing geometry between pages.
limit.markdownDescription: Maximum items in each included page. Continue using that page's next_offset; avoid editing geometry between pages.

tools.name: paint_fill_tool
tools.title: Paint Fill Tool
tools.description: Uses the fill/bucket tool to fill areas with color. In 'face' and 'element' fill modes only the face or element whose UV area contains the given texture pixel is filled, and a pixel no face covers is an error. Seeds outside the texture are rejected, and so are color and color_connected seeds outside the active layer, where the fill reads its seed color. Opacity is 0-255 regardless of Blockbench's opacity range setting.

texture_id.description: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.
texture_id.markdownDescription: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.

x.description: Texture pixel X where the fill starts; must lie inside the texture except for 'selection' and 'selected_elements' fills, which ignore it.
x.markdownDescription: Texture pixel X where the fill starts; must lie inside the texture except for 'selection' and 'selected_elements' fills, which ignore it.

y.description: Texture pixel Y where the fill starts; must lie inside the texture except for 'selection' and 'selected_elements' fills, which ignore it.
y.markdownDescription: Texture pixel Y where the fill starts; must lie inside the texture except for 'selection' and 'selected_elements' fills, which ignore it.

tolerance.description: Only zero (exact color matching) is supported by the native fill API. Nonzero tolerance is rejected.
tolerance.markdownDescription: Only zero (exact color matching) is supported by the native fill API. Nonzero tolerance is rejected.

fill_mode.description: Fill mode. 'face' and 'element' fill only the face/element whose UV area contains (x, y) in texture space (Blockbench 5.2 looks it up with UVEditor.findFaceAtUV); 'color'/'color_connected' match exact colors; 'selected_elements' fills every selected element; 'selection' fills the texture selection (image editor).
fill_mode.markdownDescription: Fill mode. 'face' and 'element' fill only the face/element whose UV area contains (x, y) in texture space (Blockbench 5.2 looks it up with UVEditor.findFaceAtUV); 'color'/'color_connected' match exact colors; 'selected_elements' fills every selected element; 'selection' fills the texture selection (image editor).

tools.description: Measures the average frames per second of Blockbench's render loop by counting rendered frames for duration_ms, then returns the average with the frame count, the fps_limit setting, Blockbench's own last-second counter, window focus at the start of the window plus whether it changed, whether the page was hidden, and whether rendering was paused. tools.description: Applies the given texture to the element with the specified ID.

id.description: ID or name of the element to apply the texture to.
id.markdownDescription: ID or name of the element to apply the texture to.

texture.description: ID or name of the texture to apply.
texture.markdownDescription: ID or name of the texture to apply.

applyTo.description: Faces that receive the texture: all (every face), blank (default; faces without a texture) or none (no face: the call only checks the element and texture and changes nothing).
applyTo.markdownDescription: Faces that receive the texture: all (every face), blank (default; faces without a texture) or none (no face: the call only checks the element and texture and changes nothing).

tools.name: add_texture_group
tools.title: Add Texture Group
tools.description: Adds a reversible texture group. All texture references must exist. Material groups require one texture per channel, either normal or height, and a color map alongside a MER map; use is_material=false for ordinary grouping.

textures.description: Array of texture IDs or names to add to the group.
textures.markdownDescription: Array of texture IDs or names to add to the group.

is_material.description: Whether the texture group is a PBR material or not.
is_material.markdownDescription: Whether the texture group is a PBR material or not.

tools.name: list_textures
tools.title: List Textures
tools.description: Returns a list of all textures in the Blockbench editor.

tools.name: get_texture
tools.title: Get Texture
tools.description: Returns the image data of the given texture or default texture.

texture.description: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.
texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID or name. If not provided, uses selected texture.

tools.name: create_pbr_material
tools.title: Create PBR Material
tools.description: Creates a new PBR material (texture group with is_material=true) and optionally assigns textures to PBR channels. Requires a PBR-capable format, distinct textures per channel, either normal or height, and a color texture alongside a MER texture. Uniform values require the corresponding map to be absent. Creation and texture moves are one undoable edit.

color_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the color (albedo) channel.
color_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the color (albedo) channel.

normal_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the normal map channel.
normal_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the normal map channel.

height_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the height/displacement map channel.
height_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the height/displacement map channel.

mer_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the MER (Metalness/Emissive/Roughness) channel.
mer_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the MER (Metalness/Emissive/Roughness) channel.

color_value.description: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture is provided.
color_value.markdownDescription: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture is provided.

mer_value.description: Uniform MER values [Metalness, Emissive, Roughness] (0-255) when no MER texture is provided.
mer_value.markdownDescription: Uniform MER values [Metalness, Emissive, Roughness] (0-255) when no MER texture is provided.

subsurface_value.description: Subsurface scattering value (0-255) for Bedrock 1.21.30+ materials.
subsurface_value.markdownDescription: Subsurface scattering value (0-255) for Bedrock 1.21.30+ materials.

tools.name: configure_material
tools.title: Configure Material
tools.description: Configures a PBR material in one undoable edit. Replaced maps are detached without deleting their textures. Use 'none' to clear a channel before using uniform values or switching between normal and height; a MER map requires a color map.

material.description: Material name or UUID to configure.
material.markdownDescription: Material name or UUID to configure.

color_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the color channel, or 'none' to use uniform color.
color_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the color channel, or 'none' to use uniform color.

normal_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the normal map, or 'none' to remove.
normal_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the normal map, or 'none' to remove.

height_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the height map, or 'none' to remove.
height_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for the height map, or 'none' to remove.

mer_texture.description: Texture ID/name for MER channel, or 'none' to use uniform values.
mer_texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID/name for MER channel, or 'none' to use uniform values.

color_value.description: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture.
color_value.markdownDescription: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture.

tools.name: list_materials
tools.title: List Materials
tools.description: Lists all PBR materials (texture groups with is_material=true) and their assigned textures per channel.

tools.name: get_material_info
tools.title: Get Material Info
tools.description: Gets detailed information about a PBR material including the compiled texture_set.json preview for Bedrock export.

tools.name: import_texture_set
tools.title: Import Texture Set
tools.description: Imports a Minecraft Bedrock texture_set.json on desktop. Validates supported JSON and decodes referenced images before one undoable edit. Returns JSON with material name/UUID and path. Reuses already loaded image paths without deleting textures. Normal and height, or MER and MERS, cannot coexist; MER images require a color image.

path.description: Path to the .texture_set.json file to import.
path.markdownDescription: Path to the .texture_set.json file to import.

tools.name: assign_texture_channel
tools.title: Assign Texture Channel
tools.description: Assigns a texture to one PBR channel in a single undoable edit. Detaches the previous map without deleting it or changing its channel. Normal and height cannot coexist; a MER map requires a color map, including in the source material after moving textures.

texture.description: Texture name or UUID to assign.
texture.markdownDescription: Texture name or UUID to assign.

channel.description: PBR channel to assign the texture to.
channel.markdownDescription: PBR channel to assign the texture to.

tools.name: save_material_config
tools.title: Save Material Config
tools.description: Saves the material's texture_set.json file to disk (Bedrock format). Requires the color texture to have a valid file path.

material.description: Material name or UUID to save.
material.markdownDescription: Material name or UUID to save.

tools.name: activate_texture
tools.title: Activate Texture
tools.description: Activates the given texture in the Blockbench texture panel so that subsequent paint operations (draw_shape_tool, paint_with_brush, gradient_tool, etc.) target it. Most paint tools already call this internally when a texture_id is provided, but you can invoke it explicitly to pin the active texture across multiple calls.

texture.description: Texture ID, UUID, or name to activate in the texture panel.
texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID, UUID, or name to activate in the texture panel.

tools.name: delete_texture
tools.title: Delete Texture
tools.description: Removes a texture from the project in one undoable edit, like deleting it from the Textures panel. Faces keep their UV mapping but lose the texture assignment, and a PBR material loses that channel, until the edit is undone. Use list_textures to find IDs.

texture.description: Texture ID, UUID, or name to remove.
texture.markdownDescription: Texture ID, UUID, or name to remove.

tools.name: trigger_action
tools.title: Trigger Action
tools.description: Triggers an available Blockbench Action and respects its condition. The native action owns Undo; only a newly opened dialog may be auto-confirmed.

action.description: Action ID from Blockbench's BarItems registry.
action.markdownDescription: Action ID from Blockbench's BarItems registry.

confirmDialog.description: Whether to confirm a newly opened dialog from this action. Existing unrelated dialogs are never confirmed.
confirmDialog.markdownDescription: Whether to confirm a newly opened dialog from this action. Existing unrelated dialogs are never confirmed.

confirmEvent.description: JSON object of MouseEvent options, with optional event type (default click).
confirmEvent.markdownDescription: JSON object of MouseEvent options, with optional event type (default click).

tools.name: risky_eval
tools.title: Eval
tools.description: Evaluates JavaScript and returns its JSON result. Does not create an Undo entry. Mutating code must manage its own correctly scoped Undo transaction; read-only evaluation leaves history unchanged.

code.description: JavaScript code to evaluate. Do not pass `console` commands or comments.
code.markdownDescription: JavaScript code to evaluate. Do not pass `console` commands or comments.

tools.name: emulate_clicks
tools.title: Emulate Clicks
tools.description: Emulates clicks on the given interface elements.

duration.description: Duration of the drag in milliseconds.
duration.markdownDescription: Duration of the drag in milliseconds.

drag.description: Drag options. If set, will perform a drag from position to 'to'.
drag.markdownDescription: Drag options. If set, will perform a drag from position to 'to'.

tools.name: fill_dialog
tools.title: Fill Dialog
tools.description: Fills the dialog with the given values.

values.description: Stringified form of values to fill the dialog with.
values.markdownDescription: Stringified form of values to fill the dialog with.

confirm.description: Whether to confirm or cancel the dialog after filling it. True to confirm, false to cancel.
confirm.markdownDescription: Whether to confirm or cancel the dialog after filling it. True to confirm, false to cancel.

tools.name: list_modes
tools.title: List Modes
tools.description: Lists Blockbench editor tabs/modes with IDs, names, native availability, and the current mode. Includes plugin-added modes. Use before set_mode to discover whether Edit, Paint, Animate, or Display is available for the current project. Camera angles are controlled separately by set_camera_angle.

tools.name: set_mode
tools.title: Set Mode
tools.description: Switches Blockbench's editor tab through its native mode trigger, respecting the mode's condition. Use mode_id='animate' to enter Animate before animation work, 'paint' before native painting tools, or 'edit' to return. Returns the resulting mode and available modes; refresh tools/list for changed tool availability. Selecting the current mode does nothing. Does not change the project's format. When the user enabled the AI Scratchpad setting, mode_id='blockwright_ai_scratchpad' relaxes the format's cube size, rotation and integer-size guardrails until another mode is selected.

mode_id.description: Mode ID returned by list_modes, such as 'edit', 'paint', 'animate', or 'display'. The Animate tab uses 'animate'. The current project must satisfy the mode's native condition.
mode_id.markdownDescription: Mode ID returned by list_modes, such as 'edit', 'paint', 'animate', or 'display'. The Animate tab uses 'animate'. The current project must satisfy the mode's native condition.

mesh_id.markdownDescription: ID or name of the mesh.

face_key.description: Face key to set UV for.
face_key.markdownDescription: Face key to set UV for.

tools.name: auto_uv_mesh
tools.title: Auto UV Mesh
tools.description: Maps only the specified/selected faces of the target mesh. project uses the active camera, unwrap projects each face to its own plane, and cylinder/sphere map around the local origin using each face's logical texture UV size (project UV size for untextured faces). mesh_id.markdownDescription: ID or name of the mesh. If not provided, uses selected mesh.

tools.name: rotate_mesh_uv
tools.title: Rotate Mesh UV
tools.description: Rotates only the target mesh's specified/selected faces around their combined UV bounding-box center, without clamping or changing selection.

tools.title: Get Cube UV
tools.description: Inspect a cube's UV mode, offset, mirroring, six face rectangles/rotations, stored and effective texture references, logical UV sizes and bitmap sizes. Read-only; no selection or preview changes.

tools.name: geckolib_get_format_info
tools.title: Get GeckoLib Format Info
tools.description: Returns the active GeckoLib project's model type, mod ID, object ID, bone and animation counts, cached export paths, and the installed plugin version. Requires the GeckoLib plugin and a GeckoLib Animated Model project.

tools.name: geckolib_set_project_settings
tools.title: Set GeckoLib Project Settings
tools.description: Sets the GeckoLib mod ID, model type and object ID on the active project. Values are validated against the plugin's namespace rules before anything is written. Does not generate the armor template rig.

errorMessage.pattern: Mod IDs may only contain lowercase letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and period.

modid.description: Mod namespace exports are written for, e.g. my_mod.
modid.markdownDescription: Mod namespace exports are written for, e.g. my_mod.

model_type.description: GeckoLib model type. Armor only records the type; it does not generate the plugin's armor template rig, which requires creating a new Armor project in Blockbench.
model_type.markdownDescription: GeckoLib model type. Armor only records the type; it does not generate the plugin's armor template rig, which requires creating a new Armor project in Blockbench.

errorMessage.pattern: Object IDs may only contain lowercase letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, period and forward slash.

model_identifier.description: Registered object ID the geometry exports as (geometry.<identifier>); may include a folder path.
model_identifier.markdownDescription: Registered object ID the geometry exports as (geometry.<identifier>); may include a folder path.

tools.name: geckolib_list_easings
tools.title: List GeckoLib Easings
tools.description: Lists every easing name GeckoLib accepts on keyframes, which of them read easingArgs, and each argument's default and meaning. Needs no project, so it can be called while planning an animation.

tools.name: geckolib_get_keyframe_easing
tools.title: Get GeckoLib Keyframe Easing
tools.description: Reads the GeckoLib easing, easing arguments and interpolation of keyframes on one bone channel, or of the current timeline selection. An easing governs the segment arriving at its keyframe, so the first keyframe of a channel is reported as inert.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.
animation_id.markdownDescription: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

bone_name.description: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.
bone_name.markdownDescription: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.

channel.description: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.
channel.markdownDescription: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.

times.description: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.
times.markdownDescription: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.

tools.name: geckolib_set_keyframe_easing
tools.title: Set GeckoLib Keyframe Easing
tools.description: Writes a GeckoLib easing (and its arguments) onto keyframes on one bone channel, or onto the current timeline selection, as one undoable edit. GeckoLib easings apply only to linear keyframes and shape the segment arriving at the keyframe they are set on, so the first keyframe of each channel is skipped and reported. Nothing in Blockbench's native keyframe API can author these.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.
animation_id.markdownDescription: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

bone_name.description: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.
bone_name.markdownDescription: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.

channel.description: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.
channel.markdownDescription: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.

times.description: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.
times.markdownDescription: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.

easing.description: GeckoLib easing name, or "none" to remove the easing and fall back to linear.
easing.markdownDescription: GeckoLib easing name, or "none" to remove the easing and fall back to linear.

easing_args.description: Arguments for the Back, Elastic, Bounce and step easings. Omit to use GeckoLib's default (1 overshoot, 0.5 bounciness, 5 steps). Ignored by every other easing.
easing_args.markdownDescription: Arguments for the Back, Elastic, Bounce and step easings. Omit to use GeckoLib's default (1 overshoot, 0.5 bounciness, 5 steps). Ignored by every other easing.

convert_interpolation.description: Set targeted keyframes to linear interpolation as part of the same edit. GeckoLib wipes easings from catmullrom, step and bezier keyframes on the next render frame, so without this the call is rejected instead of writing an easing that would not survive.
convert_interpolation.markdownDescription: Set targeted keyframes to linear interpolation as part of the same edit. GeckoLib wipes easings from catmullrom, step and bezier keyframes on the next render frame, so without this the call is rejected instead of writing an easing that would not survive.

tools.name: geckolib_reverse_keyframe_easing
tools.title: Reverse GeckoLib Keyframe Easing
tools.description: Reverses and shifts easings the way the GeckoLib plugin's handler for Blockbench's Reverse Keyframes action does: each easeIn becomes easeOut and back, every easing moves to the next later keyframe, and the first keyframe of each channel loses its easing. Use it only after keyframe times were reversed by something that left the easings in place, such as times rewritten with manage_keyframes. Do not use it after the native Reverse Keyframes action or batch_keyframe_operations reverse: with the GeckoLib plugin loaded, both already adjust the easings, so this tool would shift them a second time. It is not its own inverse; use undo to revert it.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.
animation_id.markdownDescription: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

bone_name.description: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.
bone_name.markdownDescription: Bone whose keyframes to target. Omit to act on the current timeline keyframe selection.

channel.description: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.
channel.markdownDescription: Transform channel to target. Required with bone_name, and meaningless without it.

times.description: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.
times.markdownDescription: Keyframe times in seconds. Requires bone_name; omit to target every keyframe of that channel.

tools.name: geckolib_validate_model
tools.title: Validate GeckoLib Model
tools.description: Checks the GeckoLib project against rules derived from the plugin and the GeckoLib runtime: bone-name charset and duplicates, mod ID and object ID validity, armor template bones, texture size against the UV base, and (optionally) compiled animation loop values, easing names, easing arguments and lengths. Each finding carries a stable check ID. Passing does not prove in-game correctness.

include_animations.description: Also compile the project's animations and validate their loop values, easings and lengths.
include_animations.markdownDescription: Also compile the project's animations and validate their loop values, easings and lengths.

tools.name: geckolib_export_model
tools.title: Export GeckoLib Model
tools.description: Compiles the GeckoLib geometry the plugin's model export produces, returning it as JSON and optionally writing it to a path. The text is formatted like Blockbench's own export (its JSON indentation, minify and final-newline settings). Set mode='dialog' to trigger the plugin's own export action and its save dialog instead.

mode.description: compile returns the file content without touching the UI. dialog triggers the GeckoLib plugin's own export action, which opens a native save dialog for the user to complete and updates the project's cached export path.
mode.markdownDescription: compile returns the file content without touching the UI. dialog triggers the GeckoLib plugin's own export action, which opens a native save dialog for the user to complete and updates the project's cached export path.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to write the compiled content to. Requires Blockbench filesystem permission. Only used in compile mode. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite is true.
path.markdownDescription: Absolute filesystem path to write the compiled content to. Requires Blockbench filesystem permission. Only used in compile mode. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path. Defaults to false so a re-export never silently replaces a reference file.
overwrite.markdownDescription: Replace an existing file at path. Defaults to false so a re-export never silently replaces a reference file.

max_content_length.description: Maximum characters of content to return. Use 0 to omit the content and only report its size.
max_content_length.markdownDescription: Maximum characters of content to return. Use 0 to omit the content and only report its size.

tools.name: geckolib_export_animations
tools.title: Export GeckoLib Animations
tools.description: Compiles the project's animations into GeckoLib animation-file JSON, including the easing and easingArgs the plugin writes, and optionally writes it to a path. The text is formatted like Blockbench's own export (its JSON indentation, minify and final-newline settings). resources.description: Returns information about available projects. List URIs use the slugified project name (e.g. `projects://my-character`) when unique, or `projects://<slug>~<uuid-prefix>` on collision. Reads accept UUID, exact name, or slug.

resources.name: nodes
resources.title: Blockbench Nodes
resources.description: Returns the current 3D nodes in the editor. List URIs use slugified names (e.g. `nodes://head`) when unique, with `~<uuid-prefix>` on collision. Reads accept UUID, exact name, or slug, and return the node as Blockbench saves it in a .bbmodel (its `getSaveCopy()`), plus uuid, name, type, parent (`root` or a UUID) and child UUIDs: a cube's `from`, `to` and `origin` in Blockbench units, `rotation` in degrees, faces and UVs; a mesh's vertices and faces; a group's origin and rotation. Fields Blockbench leaves out at their default are missing, such as a cube's zero rotation.

resources.name: textures
